_what: Seven Days to the Wolves — the whole programme, assembled from its acts. THE RUNNING ORDER IS CANONICAL and settled by the owner on 2026-08-12: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). docs/running-order.md is the source of truth for it; this file executes it.

_acts.0: PROLOGUE -- the main title sequence, and THE ONE ENTRY WITH NO NUMERAL. The eight act numerals are load-bearing (AGENTS.md: 'III is mrbobbytables permanently'), so a cold open in front of act I is numbered outside them rather than by renumbering everything behind it. Like act VIII it carries NO SLIDE AND NO CHAPTER MARKER: chapters() derives markers from slides, and a card announcing the main title sequence would step on the main title sequence. Picture is Nightwish's official 'Perfume Of The Timeless' music video -- see the rights note in music/bed_perfume_of_the_timeless.json, and stories/megacut/delivery.json for why it has no social copy.
_acts.I: intro — the Into the Light opener, six Guardians plated, with the title cover (wolves.jpg) covering source 24.5 - 38.
_acts.II: endlessformsmostbeautiful — delivered and credited, in the programme. Five unbroken runs of the live-action trailers scored to Nightwish's Endless Forms Most Beautiful (instrumental); The Long Walk inside them. See docs/cuts/02-endless-forms-most-beautiful.md. Its picture is a fan compilation (same provenance question as act VI, #55).
_acts.III: mrbobbytables — the August 2026 contributors piece, cut from the Curse of Osiris opening cinematic. Owner-named and owner-placed. He calls it PARTIALLY COMPLETE, so it is placed as-is and will be replaced by its finished version.
_acts.IV: kat — Kat Cosgrove's Guardian intro, behind the owner-authored BIAS FOR ACTION slide.
_acts.V: nat — Natali Vlatko's Guardian arrival, behind the same authorisation slide retitled WRONG PLACE, WRONG TIME, RIGHT ATTITUDE.
_acts.VI: 7daystothewolves — the musical. Editorial pass, delivered for review, not approved: provenance is unresolved (issue #55). Its tail plates the Cayde-6 reveal and three gold credits.
_acts.VIII: credits — the cast, 454 contributors across four projects, the comic-cover reveal at :22 and the Project Bluefin wordmark. The act that makes this the feature rather than seven eighths of it (#51).

_audio: Every act carries its own audio, unprocessed: no normaliser, no limiter, no EQ. The programme is 48 kHz STEREO because that is what the masters are -- every -hq master in Prod is stereo FLAC. The older, now-retired UPLOAD copies were AAC 5.1, but that 5.1 was the same two channels plus a derived LFE (FC/BL/BR digital silence), added by each cut's own run script. Upmixing here to recreate it would be assembly inventing a soundfield, which the audio tenet forbids; if 5.1 delivery is wanted, it belongs in the per-cut scripts that already do it. Only the six act slides are silent; a bed under them is a licensing decision.
_transitions: Issue #105, measured on v0.6 with tools/transitions.py (all times programme clock): every act entered DRY out of the slides' digital silence (4-14 s of -inf per join), the worst being act VII at -15.3 dB one second after the slide, and acts I and III ended HOT against the silence (-24.4 and -14.8 dB in their last second). The treatment below is explicit afade shapes, stated here so they are reproducible: fade_in 2.0 s on every act that starts behind a slide, fade_out 2.0 s on the acts whose tails do not already fade (I, III, V) and 3.0 s on act VII so the programme lands rather than stops. Acts II and VI fade themselves out (measured -96.7 / -90.3 dB in their last seconds) and carry no fade_out; the IV->V join is direct and continuous (-15.2 -> -11.9 dB) and carries no fade on either side. All fade times are ACT FILM time -- the clip's own clock -- so a re-order never moves them. LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): (1) whether the slides carry a bed or room tone -- a licensing decision, per the megacut skill; (2) levelling the act ENTRIES, which still differ by ~20 dB (act III at -29.5 vs act VII at -15.3) -- static gain per act is a mix decision; (3) how long the slides' silence should be. THE 15 s IV-V SLIDE IS GONE (v2.2): with the Perfume thread running through the show, a 15 s frozen card in silence after movement 3's static skull shot was about twenty seconds in which nothing moved. It holds 5.0 s now, like every other slide, and movement 3's fade_out is 1.0 s rather than 2.0 so the music carries closer to the card. PROLOGUE JOIN, measured 2026-08-14 on the built act rather than assumed: the prologue's own tail runs -28.3 -> -34.8 -> -58.7 dB RMS across its last three seconds (the song fading under the bridge from 93.000), and act I opens at digital silence (-127 dB) climbing through -30 to -18 dB. So the join needs NO fade on either side and carries none: the prologue fades itself out, exactly as acts II and VI do, and act I's own quiet opening picks it up. A fade_out here would double the taper on a fade the act already performs. ONE EDITORIAL FINDING, LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): the bridge exists because the owner asked for the wallpaper to 'replace the black part', and act I's 5 s silent slide immediately after it puts a black part back. It reads as a continuous darkening today -- night fades to black and the slide rises out of the same darkness, which is how a title sequence normally hands to act one -- but if the intent was for the wallpaper to hand STRAIGHT into a film, the fix is to drop or restyle act I's slide, and a slide is the one thing this show gives every act. Not changed unilaterally.

items._gain: Owner-approved 2026-08-14 (#164): act I measured -19.4 LUFS integrated where the other six acts cluster -9.7..-11.3, so the show opened ~9 dB quiet and jumped at the I->II join. Its true peak is -4.6 dBTP (re-measured on the delivered master before choosing this number), so +3.5 dB is the MOST a plain gain can add while staying inside the house -0.9..-1.1 dBTP band -- the audio tenet forbids a limiter, so the remaining ~5.6 LU needs a re-master of the act and is recorded on #164. items._trim: Owner 2026-08-14 (alpha QA): '28:20 has extra fade out that can be cut, including the music video director text, transition when the camera is in the ship make the song fade out but not too much then punch them with the credits at the end.' MEASURED: 28:20 programme time is movement 5's own tail. The in-ship shot (camera inside the sunken wreck, light through the hull) dissolves out from ~109.5; the source's burned credits ('(c) A LOVELY BUNCH OF COCONUTS 2024 / DIRECTED BY VILLE LIPIAINEN') fade in from 111.0 and are readable by 111.5, then near-black, then a held interior to EOF at 117.221 -- there is no shot boundary >=0.15 after film 100, it is one long dissolve, so the point is chosen on the frames: 109.5 is the last moment the camera still reads as IN the ship, with zero text risk. trim_to 109.5 cuts all of it; the 1.5 s fade_out lands against the AUTHORED end (st 108.0), which is 'fade out but not too much' from a -20 dB mean bed; act VIII's fade_in stays 0.0 so the drum smash punches on the next frame. Cuts 7.7 s of programme.
items._no_fade_in: Owner 2026-08-14: '27:03 transition needs a dramatic analysis, very close.' Measured what is actually there: Europa ends on the Europa/Jupiter vista behind the KubeCon card and fades to black over its last half second; movement 5 then opens on a DARK EARTH LIMB (Y~24) that holds 3.504 s before the sun bursts over the curve (Y jumps to 93), then an ice plume at 4.505, and at 6.506 -- programme 27:02.3, the frame the owner marked -- the cut to the body sinking through deep blue water. Vertical motion was measured on both sides and there is NO pan: the join is dark-to-dark, not a tilt. So the problem was never the frame, it was that a 2.0 s fade IN under an already near-black 3.5 s shot, coming off a 3.0 s fade OUT, made about four seconds of nothing exactly where the film wants to hold its breath. Dropping the fade puts the song in at full level on the cut, so the dark limb becomes a held breath with music under it and the sunrise lands as the payoff. v2.3 goes further on the other side of the join: act VII now ends on the eclipse at full brightness (its trim note has the numbers), so the held-breath limb follows a hard picture cut rather than a fade.
items._still_open: The B alternative -- movement 5 opening on the meteor strike at source 393.560, movement 4 extended to keep the song gapless -- is rendered as an excerpt beside the A default (renders/review/). Owner picks off the excerpts: #192.

items._thread: Movement 5 of 5, and the end of the song. The owner asked to 'match the transition panning up from laura after europa'. MEASURED, AND THE PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE: there is no pan on either side. Europa's tail is the Europa/Jupiter vista behind the KubeCon card, fading to black, and movement 5 opens on a static dark Earth limb -- vertical displacement is 0 px across both, by row-profile correlation. What the join actually is, and what it is good at, is dark-to-dark: one world in space goes out, another comes up, and 3.5 s later the sun breaks over it. Act VII is never shortened to make anything FIT (#178) -- the v2.3 trim on it is not a fit, it is the owner's own eclipse note.

items.label: Act VIII — Credits
items._what: NO ACT SLIDE, by owner instruction: 'no credits slide, go right to the metal ... it should surprise the viewer.' Every other act is announced by a card; this one is not. Europa fades to black on its own tail and the drum smash lands on the next frame. The missing slide also removes act VIII's CHAPTER MARKER -- chapters() derives them from slides -- and that is the point rather than a side effect: a 'VIII. Credits' entry on the scrub bar would spoil the same surprise the cut is built to land. fade_in is 0.0 so nothing eases in front of the smash.

_chapters: Each act slide carries the audience-facing `chapter` title; `python3 tools/megacut.py <plan> --chapters` derives the timestamps from this plan's own clock, so the markers can never drift from the running order. The numeral is part of the title because the show is told in numbered acts. Act VIII has no slide, so it has no marker -- that is the ambush working as designed. AS OF v2.1 ACT VII HAS NONE EITHER: the owner asked for its title slide to go so movement 4 could hard-cut into Europa, and the marker went with the slide. Six published entries, not eight. If Europa should keep a scrub-bar entry without a card in front of it, chapters() would need to read a `chapter` off the CLIP -- a change nobody has asked for yet.
